Shri Jitendra Kumar Gupta- Advocate for respondents No.3
 Shri Bal Krishna Agrawal- Advocate for respondent/Insura
 Order

The present appeal has been filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, assailing the award dated 20.12.2023 passed by the 14th Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 846/2019, limited to the extent of distribution of the compensation amount amongst the claimants.
2. The date of accident, negligence, and liability are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Rakesh Shivhare in a motor accident, compensation to the tune of Rs.21,18,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization was awarded.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the impugned award is contrary to settled principles of law, inasmuch as the appellant, being the legally wedded wife of the deceased, has been awarded only 30% share of the compensation.
It was further contended that respondents Nos. 3 to 5 acted mala fide by filing a separate NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4628 2 MA-1673-2024 claim petition excluding the appellant.

It was also argued that respondent No. 3 is a Smt. Rani Shivhare vs Heeralal Mali on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70099256/
1 pensioner and respondents Nos. 4 and 5 are major and self-sufficient, therefore allocation of substantial share in their favour is erroneous and warrants interference.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award.
5 . Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the misc. appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.

On perusal of the record, it is evident that the Claims Tribunal has distributed the compensation amount by awarding 30% share to the appellant, 30% each to respondents Nos. 4 and 5, and 10% to respondent No. 3.
The Tribunal has exercised its discretion after considering the relationship of the claimants with the deceased and their dependency.
8. This Court finds no perversity, illegality, or arbitrariness in the manner of distribution of the compensation amount.
The discretion exercised by the Claims Tribunal in apportioning the compensation cannot be said to be unjust or contrary to law so as to warrant interference by this Court in appellate jurisdiction.
9. Consequently, the appeal being devoid of merit deserves to be dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
